craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as mirror-needing-only-mind; vyabhicāri clarity of mind-proven reflection (C1 rasa block). Sanskrit-first: yadi…cet…tadā (IF…THEN — protasis long, apodosis certain); manasā eva siddhe (proved BY MIND ALONE — eva restricts the proof); na…anyathā (no OTHER cause — total exclusion closes). Rows: 2 (bimba-pratibimba unpacked: ‘reflection — image-making, with its original’ spilling down the line), 1 (‘at all’ end-weighted — totality), 5 (conditional tread: long supposing line, short necessity line). Rupture: ‘then’ (supposition turns to necessity). Rejected: ‘picture’ for reflection — killed: pratibimba is technical (counter-image); ‘for free’ wordplay on free consciousness — killed: pun smuggling doctrine (svatantra ≠ gratis). Read aloud: IF, in a MIR-ror's BEL-ly … WERE-proved BY-mind a-LONE — THEN, with-IN the MIR-ror OF-free CON-scious-ness … NO-o-ther-CAUSE at-ALL.

lines: If, in a mirror’s belly, a reflection — image-making, with its original — were proved by mind alone —
then, within the mirror of free consciousness, things have no other cause at all.
l4.sanskrit_cite: ādarśakukṣau pratibimbakāri sabimbakaṃ syād yadi mānasiddham | svacchandasaṃvinmukhuraantarāle bhāveṣu hetvantaram asti nānyat

reads_against.argmap: If even a common mirror shows prototype-with-reflection as mind-established, the free-consciousness mirror needs no other cause among things. → A fortiori: mind-proven reflection needs no second cause.
